title: Tuna noodle casserole
subtitle: Classic American tuna and egg noodle bake
excerpt: Egg noodles, tinned tuna, frozen peas, and cream of mushroom sauce baked with a crispy breadcrumb topping. The archetypal American midweek casserole, quick to assemble and deeply comforting.
sourceNotes: Tuna noodle casserole became a mid-twentieth-century American staple after the development of condensed cream of mushroom soup by Campbell's in the 1930s. The dish is documented in Joy of Cooking and in virtually every American regional and community cookbook from the 1950s onwards. Its convenience-food base (tinned tuna, tinned soup, frozen peas) made it the defining American casserole of the era.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding the breadcrumb topping. Defrost overnight, add the topping, and bake from cold at 180°C for 35 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the day before without the topping. Add the topping and bake just before serving.

content.text: Tuna noodle casserole is one of those dishes that exists in the gap between cooking and assembling. It takes 15 minutes to put together and 30 minutes in the oven, and it feeds six people with almost no effort. The from-scratch version, using a real cream-of-mushroom sauce rather than tinned soup, is noticeably better.
Cook the egg noodles in well-salted boiling water for 1 minute less than the packet time. Drain and set aside. Heat the oven to 180°C (fan 160°C).

Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes, add the mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the flour and stir for 1 minute. Gradually add the milk and stock, stirring constantly. Simmer for 5 minutes until thickened. Season generously.
Remove from the heat. Add the drained noodles, tuna, and frozen peas. Stir to combine. Pour into a buttered baking dish.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the melted butter and scatter over the top. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and bubbling. Leave to rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.cause: Noodles absorbed all the sauce before baking
items.fix: Make the sauce slightly thinner (use an extra 100 ml of milk) to account for the noodles continuing to absorb liquid in the oven.

content.text: Tuna noodle casserole is the canonical American casserole. It is fast and cheap. It uses tins and frozen vegetables and feeds a family from a single dish. Its popularity peaked in the 1950s and 1960s. Convenience-food manufacturers were actively promoting dishes built around their products. Green bean casserole and sweet potato casserole come from the same era. Tuna noodle casserole endures because it works.
